newsitem.title: USA: CBS says GOP got foreign funds too -- in 1992.
newsitem.headline: CBS says GOP got foreign funds too -- in 1992.

text.p: American businessman Michael Kojima, who made a $500,000 donation to the Republican Party in 1992, funnelled in the money from Japanese businessmen who sought to profit from Republican connections, CBS Evening News reported Monday.
The CBS report came on the eve of a potentially explosive Senate investigation of President Bill Clinton's campaign ties to foreign money.
One top priority is to determine whether China or other foreign interests sought to influence U.S. foreign policy by making large donations to Democrats in the 1996 campaign.

The CBS report said Kojima flew in a group of Japanese businessmen for the 1992 Republican fundraiser after asking them for hundreds of thousands of dollars for the chance to meet President George Bush.
CBS said it interviewed some of the businessmen in Japan and they indicated they were the source for at least some of Kojima's GOP donation.
CBS said when Kojima's $500,000 donation made headlines in 1992, a shocked ex-wife exposed him as a deadbeat dad saying he owed her more than $100,000 in child support.
CBS added: "One final note: The GOP fought Kojima's wives, children and other creditors in court for the $500,000 donation -- and wound up keeping about half of it."
